To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of a combination of artificial EEG trials, obtained by relevant combinations of the original trials available, and of the original trials themselves, enables us to significantly reduce BCI calibration times, and (ii) the proposed fast user-to-user transfer approach is very efficient to reduce calibration time.

(1) the use of artificial EEG trials can reduce the calibration time of BCI by 50% or even more, and (2) the use of user-to-user transfer can reduce the calibration by 30%, but this is only the case if a sufficient number of other users are available.

1) the best way to reduce BCI calibra- tion time is by using artificial EEG trials, 2) a good way to do so is by using a combination of the different approaches proposed, and 3) a good way of generating artificial EEG trials is by using a method that combines and distorts the available EEG trials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reducing the calibration time of BCI.
the design of fast, robust, and accurate algorithms for the detection of oscillatory activity in the brain, which can be used in BCI.
the design of signal processing approaches to minimize calibration time for oscillatory activity-based BCI.

the best approach to reduce or suppress BCI calibration time is to combine the different approaches proposed in this paper.
